historical_references.reference: Arjuna, also known as Arjuna the Invincible or Arjaj, was a central character in the Indian epic Mahabharata. He was the third of the five Pandava brothers and was considered to be one of the greatest warriors in Indian history. Arjuna was the husband of Draupadi and the charioteer of Lord Krishna during the Mahabharata war.

Arjun is also mentioned in the Puranas, a set of eighteen major Sanskrit texts in Hinduism, as a great archer and devotee of Lord Shiva. It is said that Arjuna gained the Pasupata Astra, a powerful weapon from Lord Shiva, by performing severe penance and austerities.
